@graph.headline: Vitreous Humour: Anatomy, Function and PVD
@graph.description: Revise vitreous humour anatomy, composition, attachments, ageing, PVD, vitreomacular traction and surgical relevance with tables and MCQs.

mainEntity.name: What is the main function of the vitreous humour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The vitreous provides a transparent optical path and a hydrated mechanical matrix. It also permits molecular diffusion and influences adhesion between the posterior cortex and retina.

mainEntity.name: What is the vitreous humour made of?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is 98 to 99.7% water with a sparse matrix of collagen and hyaluronan. Type II collagen is the predominant fibrillar collagen.

mainEntity.name: What is the strongest vitreous attachment?

acceptedAnswer.text: The vitreous base, which straddles the ora serrata, is the strongest vitreoretinal attachment.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between synchysis and syneresis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Synchysis is liquefaction of vitreous gel. Syneresis is aggregation and collapse of the remaining gel.

mainEntity.name: Why does PVD sometimes cause a retinal tear?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focal adhesion can remain fixed while surrounding vitreous moves, concentrating traction on the retina and producing a break.
